chapter: Paris, the Blackbirds and Noble Sissle
title: Bass Edwards's cigar; trying to find Sissle in 1974
summary: Bass Edwards played tuba with a cigar smoking through the bell; Briggs tells of failing to reach the ailing Sissle in 1974 and defends his band from a critic's Uncle Tom charge.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Yes, sure. You see smoke comes out through the bell. He was quite an attraction, and we had -- I really have a very wonderful souvenir of Noble Sissle and my only regret was that when I went back to the States in '74, I -- I did everything to contact him, he was not at the address that I had.
But I was informed by phone after
going to the address about three or four times, I finally called, and someone answered saying that Mr. Sissle was very, very ill, and he was in Miami, Florida.
So I said, 'Could you give me an address,' and she said, 'I will try to get the address from Mr. -- from one of his sons.' That was new to me. I knew he had one son, but that was new to me.
She said, 'I'll try to get the address from one of his sons, and give me your phone number and I'll phone and let you know.'
So, having heard no news from him, I wrote the letter to the same address, the address that I had, asking to forward the letter on to his present address. But I never had any news.
The only news I had is when he passed away and friends of his told me. I think Herb, if I'm not mistaken,
Herb Fleming told me. Herb Fleming told me he passed, and he had a terrific funeral. He was a big Mason, you know.
He had a wonderful funeral. But I had a wonderful souvenir of Mr. Sissle, because Mr. Sissle knew, he was not what you'd call a musician, and he didn't try to say that he was.

And I had heard of certain musicians -- I won't mention the names--- it was recently, who made remarks saying that -- one of them wrote a book even, and he said, Noble Sissle's band was Uncle Tom and that, you see, he said that the music was awful, they was just corny, and --
Well, I, having played with Noble Sissle, I'd say, that guy, I don't know how he got into Noble's band. I won't mention his name. I don't know how he got into Noble's band.
